cues.en: Orbital rings represent one of the best ways to get people off a planet. They also happen to be handy if you want to build a planet too.
cues.zh: 轨道环是让人离开星球的最佳方式之一。如果你想建造一颗星球，它们也正好派得上用场。

cues.en: So today's topic, Orbital Rings, is the culmination of this series, especially the concepts we've discussed in the last two episodes,
cues.zh: 所以今天的主题——轨道环——是这个系列的收官，尤其是我们过去两集讨论的那些概念，

cues.en: Launch Loops and Space Towers.
cues.zh: 发射环和太空塔。

cues.en: You don't have to have seen those first, but I spent more time explaining the basic concept of active support in those.
cues.zh: 你不必先看那两集，但我在那两集里花了更多时间解释主动支撑的基本概念。

cues.en: The Orbital Ring has so many applications
cues.zh: 轨道环的应用太多了，

cues.en: I didn't want to spend much time repeating the basic physical concepts in favor of exploring those.
cues.zh: 所以我不想花太多时间重复基本物理概念，而是更想探讨这些应用。

cues.en: I've talked in passing about the Orbital Ring before, indeed we covered it briefly in one of the oldest episodes on this channel, and I regret being brief there because we bypass so many of the uses these things have.
cues.zh: 我以前顺带提过轨道环；其实在本频道最早的一些节目里，我们简单讲过它。我后悔当时讲得太简略，因为那样就略过了它的许多用途。

cues.en: This series has been mainly focused on getting into space cheaper and safer,
cues.zh: 这个系列主要关注的是更便宜、更安全地进入太空，

cues.en: and we have discussed some systems that are so much cheaper that they can be used to get people up into space at prices that make it affordable for an average person to take a vacation up in space. The Orbital Ring goes far beyond permitting more scientific research or expensive vacations though.
cues.zh: 我们也讨论过一些系统，它们便宜得多，甚至能以普通人负担得起太空度假的价格把人送上太空。不过，轨道环远不止能支持更多科学研究或昂贵的度假。

cues.en: It is a system that genuinely allows people to commute to space for work in the morning and still come home for dinner and spend no more for a ticket to orbit than you would for a train or plane ticket to a neighboring city.
cues.zh: 这个系统真正能让人早上通勤到太空上班，晚上还能回家吃晚饭，而且去轨道的票价不会比去邻市的火车票或机票更贵。

cues.en: We've discussed the concept of active support and dynamic structures before and in a good deal of detail in the last couple episodes of this series, so I will keep the review this time brief.
cues.zh: 我们之前讨论过主动支撑和动态结构的概念，而且在这个系列最近几集里讲得相当详细，所以这次我会简短回顾。

cues.en: Normally, materials provide passive support,
cues.zh: 通常，材料提供的是被动支撑，

cues.en: the forces which bind molecules together or keep them apart keep a material from ripping apart under tension or smashing together under compression.
cues.zh: 使分子结合或彼此分开的力，让材料在受拉时不会撕裂，在受压时不会压溃。

cues.en: Some materials are stronger than others. It is very easy to rip apart tissue paper and far harder to tear apart Kevlar.
cues.zh: 有些材料比其他材料更强。撕开薄纸很容易，撕开凯夫拉则难得多。

cues.en: But even super materials like carbon nanotubes and graphene have their limits and we have yet to mass produce them.
cues.zh: 但即便是碳纳米管和石墨烯这样的超级材料也有极限，而且我们还没能大规模生产它们。

cues.en: We have an alternative way to hold stuff up though, we can push on it. That's what keeps a sheet of paper hovering over an air vent or helicopter hovering in the air. In the last episode, we looked at keeping things in place by bouncing materials
cues.zh: 不过，我们还有另一种把东西撑住的方法：我们可以对它施加推力。纸片能在通风口上方悬停、直升机能在空中悬停，靠的就是这一点。上一集里，我们研究了如何通过让材料

cues.en: upward inside them, allowing super tall structures.
cues.zh: 在内部向上反弹来把东西固定住，从而支撑起超高的结构。

cues.en: But the Orbital Ring uses a different method more akin to what we saw in the Lofstrom Loop, but still a bit different.
cues.zh: 但轨道环使用一种不同的方法，更接近我们在 Lofstrom Loop 中看到的方式，但仍有些不同。

cues.en: When I place something in a stable circular orbit, it has a speed based on the mass of the object it is orbiting and the distance it is orbiting at.
cues.zh: 当我把某个物体放入稳定的圆形轨道时，它的速度取决于它所环绕物体的质量和它所在的轨道距离。

cues.en: That's around eight kilometers or five miles per second for the area of space just above our atmosphere.
cues.zh: 在大气层正上方的近地空间，这个速度大约是每秒八公里或五英里。

cues.en: It actually drops as you get further away, just three kilometers a second when you get out to geostationary
cues.zh: 随着距离变远，速度其实会下降，到了地球静止轨道的

cues.en: distances,
cues.zh: 距离，

cues.en: slow enough that you orbit at the same speed the Earth turns on its axis, so that you stay above the same point.
cues.zh: 就只有每秒三公里，这足够慢，让你绕轨道运行的速度和地球自转一致，从而始终停留在同一个地点上方。

cues.en: Further out, at the Moon, the speed is about one kilometer per second and drops the farther you go until you are no longer bound to Earth gravitationally.
cues.zh: 再往外，在月球位置，速度大约是每秒一公里，越远越慢，直到你不再受到地球引力的束缚。

cues.en: We haven't been much interested in this series with space beyond low orbit, let alone beyond geostationary,
cues.zh: 在这个系列里，我们之前对低轨道以外的太空不太感兴趣，更别说地球静止轨道之外了，

cues.en: but we are today, so keep that in mind.
cues.zh: 但今天我们很感兴趣，所以请记住这一点。

cues.en: It's the speed that matters, not the angle. You can orbit Earth around the Equator or from pole to pole at the same speed. But each orbital path is a unique thing and any object on that same path with that same speed won't seem to move relative to anything else on that path.
cues.zh: 关键在于速度，而不是角度。你可以以同样的速度沿着赤道或从两极绕地球运行。但每条轨道都是独一无二的，在同一条轨道上以相同速度运行的物体，彼此之间看起来都是静止的。

cues.en: Which means if I'm in orbit of the Earth in a space suit and let go of a flashlight I was holding onto, it will seem to just sit there next to me, unless I gave it a little shove in which case it would drift away.
cues.zh: 这意味着，如果我穿着宇航服在地球轨道上，放开手里拿的手电筒，它看起来就会停在我身边，除非我推它一下，它才会飘走。

cues.en: So I could put several objects in the same orbital path and they'd sit there together unmoving relative to each other. They'd still be zipping around the Earth at high speed but then so are you and everything in your home, zipping around the planet and on the planet around the Sun and around the galactic core too.
cues.zh: 所以我可以把几个物体放在同一条轨道上，它们相对彼此就是静止不动的。它们仍然在高速绕着地球飞驰，但你和家里的一切也是如此——绕着地球飞驰，跟着地球绕太阳转，还绕着银河系中心转。

cues.en: Everything is moving but it is relative motion.
cues.zh: 一切都在运动，但这都是相对运动。

cues.en: If I were standing on one of those objects, I could lay a bridge down to the next and walk over just fine, though since we are in free fall, I'd basically float not walk.
cues.zh: 如果我站在其中一个物体上，完全可以搭一座桥通往下一个物体走过去，不过由于处于自由落体状态，我基本上是漂浮过去而不是走过去。

cues.en: I could extend this all the way around the orbital path as a big ring.
cues.zh: 我可以沿着整条轨道一直延伸，连成一个巨大的圆环。

cues.en: This orbiting ring would travel around just fine,
cues.zh: 这个轨道环可以正常运转，

cues.en: but it is not much use to us as is.
cues.zh: 但就目前这样对我们没多大用处。

cues.en: On that same note, if I had a perfectly rigid material,
cues.zh: 同理，如果我有一种完全刚性的材料，

cues.en: I could construct a ring out of it around the Earth and it would just hang there even without orbiting because all the gravity on it would cancel out. This would be quite useful since it would be stationary to the ground if unstable.
cues.zh: 我就能用它围绕地球建一个圆环，哪怕不绕轨运行，它也能悬在那里，因为各处受到的引力会相互抵消。这会非常有用，因为虽然不稳定，但它相对于地面是静止的。

cues.en: Also, we have no perfectly rigid material so it would sag down to the planet.
cues.zh: 此外，我们并没有完全刚性的材料，所以它会向下塌陷到地球上。

cues.en: The one orbiting would not since it experiences no gravity, or rather its inertia or centrifugal force cancels that gravity out. It is also technically unstable,
cues.zh: 而轨道运行中的圆环就不会塌陷，因为它处于零重力状态，或者说它的惯性或离心力抵消了引力。严格来说它也是不稳定的，

cues.en: but we can fix that and in a way that makes it more useful too. We'll get to that shortly.
cues.zh: 但我们可以解决这个问题，而且还能让它变得更有用。我们稍后会讲到。

cues.en: So far so good though. I could make a nice metal hoop around the planet, and if it was spinning at orbital velocity it would stay in place.
cues.zh: 不过目前为止进展顺利。我可以围绕地球做一个金属圆环，只要它以轨道速度旋转，就能保持在原位。

cues.en: Now imagine for the moment we stuck a bunch of magnets on this metal hoop. Actually, since it is a big piece of metal, we probably wouldn't need to put any magnets in it, just run electric current through it, but let's keep it conceptually simple for now. The ring has a bunch of magnets on it. Now I build a big space tower next to it like the ones we discussed last episode, and I reach out and put a magnet over some spot on the spinning hoop.
cues.zh: 现在想象一下，我们在金属环上贴了一堆磁铁。其实因为它是块大金属，可能根本不需要放磁铁，通电就行，但为了概念简单起见先这么想。圆环上贴了一堆磁铁。现在我在它旁边建一座巨大的太空塔，就像上期讨论过的那种，然后我伸手在旋转的圆环某处放上一块磁铁。

cues.en: The hoop is spinning around very fast, whereas I'm stationary to the Earth, so if I touched it, that hoop would slice through me like circular saw. But it won't be touching that magnet,
cues.zh: 圆环转得极快，而我相对于地球是静止的，所以如果我碰到它，它会像电圆锯一样把我切开。但它并不会碰到那块磁铁，

cues.en: the magnets on the hoop will be pushing back against it.
cues.zh: 圆环上的磁铁会产生推力排斥它。

cues.en: That's not terribly stable, but if I took a bracelet with magnets on it and opened it up and clapped it around the orbiting ring, it would just hover there. If I put some more on, they'd hover there too, and I could put some platform there and stand on it.
cues.zh: 这不太稳定，但如果我拿一个带磁铁的手镯，打开它并扣在轨道环周围，它就会直接悬浮在那里。如果我多放几个，它们也会悬浮着，我甚至可以在上面搭个平台站上去。

cues.en: This would be different than before,
cues.zh: 这和之前不同，

cues.en: because before all those objects were in orbit too. These are just hanging right over the Earth. The ring is orbiting but they are not. So when I stand on my platform,
cues.zh: 因为之前所有物体也都在轨道上运行。而这些只是悬挂在地球正上方。圆环在绕轨运行，但它们没有。所以当我站在平台上时，

cues.en: I feel gravity, almost as much as on Earth. I could take this bracelet and extend it around the ring to make a second ring around my orbiting ring, and it would not be moving relative to Earth. I could walk around the entire thing just like I was on Earth only high up, nowhere and gravity is a bit weaker.
cues.zh: 我能感受到重力，几乎和在地球表面一样强。我可以把这个手镯延伸一圈，围绕轨道环做成第二个环，而且它相对于地球是静止不动的。我可以在整座环上行走，就像在地球上一样，只是身处高空虚空之中，且重力稍弱一点。

cues.en: I could even build an airtight house up there. As I added weight though, I noticed the orbiting ring was beginning to sag a bit. See that ring has just enough momentum to stay in place, in orbit, on its own. Now I'm adding mass that isn't moving, has no momentum,
cues.zh: 我甚至可以在上面建一座气密房屋。不过随着我增加重量，我发现轨道环开始有点下沉了。要知道，那个环自身的动量刚好足够让它维持在轨道位置。现在我增加了不动的质量，它们没有任何动量，

cues.en: and the system, the orbiting part plus the stationary part, needs to have enough momentum to stay in orbit.
cues.zh: 而整个系统——轨道运行部分加上静止部分——必须有足够的动量才能维持在轨道上。

cues.en: I could go ahead and get my stationary parts up to orbital speed, fixing the problem, but that kinda defeats the purpose.
cues.zh: 我当然可以把静止部分加速到轨道速度来解决问题，但这有点违背初衷了。

cues.en: Instead, I can add more momentum to the ring, speed it up a bit beyond normal
cues.zh: 相反，我可以给圆环增加更多动量，让它的速度稍微超过正常

cues.en: velocity, now the whole system has just the right momentum to stay in orbit even though the orbiting ring has a bit too much and the stationary part not enough.
cues.zh: 轨道速度，现在整个系统就有了恰到好处的动量来维持轨道，尽管轨道环的动量稍显过剩，而静止部分则动量不足。

cues.en: This is the basic concept.
cues.zh: 这就是基本概念。

cues.en: I take a hoop of metal a millimeter thick or a kilometer thick and spin it around the planet at orbital speed.
cues.zh: 我拿一个哪怕只有一毫米厚、或有一公里厚的金属环，以轨道速度绕着行星旋转。

cues.en: If I run some current through it to make it a magnet or am using a ferromagnetic material like iron or nickel, I can now float things over it by spinning the ring a little faster.
cues.zh: 如果我给它通电让它变成磁铁，或者使用铁、镍等铁磁性材料，现在只要让环转得稍快一点，就能让物体悬浮在它上方。

cues.en: The circumference of Earth is just over 40,000,000 meters, so if I made such a hoop out of a standard thin wire, say 25 grams a meter, that hoop would weigh a million kilograms.
cues.zh: 地球周长刚超过4000万米，所以如果用标准的细线（比如每米25克）做这样一个环，整个环的重量将达到100万公斤。

cues.en: Way too much for a single rocket to lift up, but you can bring it up in segments and solder it together, it's just wire.
cues.zh: 单枚火箭根本抬不动这么多，但你可以分段送上去再焊接起来，反正只是导线。

cues.en: Indeed we can fly up next to it and add more wire, more strands,
cues.zh: 确实，我们可以飞到它旁边，加更多导线、更多股线，

cues.en: since if we're in orbit it just seems to be hanging there, so we can add to it as we want.
cues.zh: 因为在轨道上，它看起来就像悬在那儿，所以我们可以想加多少就加多少。

cues.en: We can also spin it faster to let us add more weight suspended above or around it.
cues.zh: 我们还可以让它转得更快，从而在它上方或周围悬挂更多重量。

cues.en: Now a spinning ring that we start spinning faster than orbital speed is going to have more centrifugal force added to it, and if we get enough of that it will rip the ring apart.
cues.zh: 现在，如果让一个旋转环的转速超过轨道速度，它受到的离心力就会更大；一旦离心力足够大，就会把环撕碎。

cues.en: But for the moment we have a spinning ring inside a stationary pipe that's magnetically kept afloat from touching it.
cues.zh: 但此刻，我们有一个旋转环，位于一根静止的管道内，靠磁力悬浮，避免接触管壁。

cues.en: That ring is over 40,000 kilometers long, the rough circumference of the Earth. A space elevator is about the same length and unlike a space elevator,
cues.zh: 这个环长超过4万公里，大致相当于地球周长。太空电梯长度差不多，但与太空电梯不同，

cues.en: this is just wire, plain regular old wire, nothing special about it.
cues.zh: 这只是一根导线，普普通通的老式导线，没什么特别。

cues.en: Nothing special about the conduit around it either, except that it's got magnets on it and we can make those electromagnets
cues.zh: 它外面的导管也没什么特别，只是上面装有磁体，而我们可以把这些做成电磁铁，

cues.en: so that we can run power through them and use that to speed the ring inside up or slow it down if we need to add or subtract weight from the whole thing. We can hang some solar panels off to the side attached to the conduit to provide for that.
cues.zh: 这样就能给它们通电，用电流让里面的环加速或减速——当我们需要给整个装置增减重量时。我们可以把一些太阳能板挂在导管侧面，为此供电。

cues.en: We now have a solid ring in space, not seeming to move relative to the ground below,
cues.zh: 现在我们在太空中有了一个实心环，相对于下方地面似乎不动，

cues.en: with a power source that can let us add weight to it.
cues.zh: 还有一个电源，能让我们给它增加重量。

cues.en: Now the outside isn't moving relative to the surface of the Earth, so we could have this at pretty much any altitude we wanted, one of these would work just over the ground, but we will say it's about 80 kilometers up, same as the Lofstrom Loop. We could drop a rope down from there and someone could climb up from the ground.
cues.zh: 现在外侧相对于地球表面不动，所以我们几乎可以把它放在任意高度；这种装置在地面正上方也能运行，但我们姑且说它在约80公里高处，和 Lofstrom Loop 一样。我们可以从那里放一根绳子下来，让人从地面爬上去。

cues.en: Now a regular rope couldn't handle that and no one could climb that, but we have plenty of fairly mundane substances
cues.zh: 普通绳子承受不了，也没人能爬上去，但我们有很多相当普通的材料，

cues.en: that do have a breaking limit of more than 80 kilometers.
cues.zh: 它们的断裂长度确实超过80公里。

cues.en: We're not sure if stuff like graphene can handle going up tens of thousands of kilometers but we've got plenty that can handle tens or hundreds of kilometers.
cues.zh: 我们不确定石墨烯这类材料能否撑到数万公里高，但有很多材料能撑几十或几百公里。

cues.en: This includes those that can handle having current run through them or are strong enough to let us bolt some wire to them at least.
cues.zh: 其中包括能承受电流通过的，或至少强度足以让我们把导线固定上去的。

cues.en: So we drop a cable down to Earth with a wire in it, and some elevator with an electric motor grabs that cable and its power cord and uses that to pull itself up to the ring. Power can be supplied by some other solar panels up on the ring or down on the planet.
cues.zh: 于是我们向地球放下一根缆绳，里面带导线；某个装电动机的升降舱抓住这根缆绳和它的电源线，靠它把自己拉到环上。电力可以由环上或地面上的其他太阳能板提供。

cues.en: Even without superconductors,
cues.zh: 即使没有超导体，

cues.en: we can run an electric cable 80 kilometers without losing too much power. Which conveniently means we can run power from all those solar panels on the ring where there are no cloudy days down to Earth too,
cues.zh: 我们也能把电缆拉80公里而不损失太多电力。这正好意味着，我们还能把环上那些没有阴雨天的太阳能板的电力一路送到地球，

cues.en: but never mind that for now.
cues.zh: 不过先别管这个。

cues.en: This is the basic orbital ring, it can be scaled up. You can make thicker rings or add more rings right next to it, though in practice you'd want to have every other one spinning backwards in retrograde orbit.
cues.zh: 这是基础的轨道环，规模还可以继续扩大。你可以把环做得更厚，或在旁边并排增加更多环，不过实际上你会希望相邻的环以逆行轨道反向旋转。

cues.en: They wobble too, so rather than running cables straight down, you'd often want to angle them like guy wires.
cues.zh: 它们也会晃动，所以与其把缆绳垂直向下牵引，通常更需要像防风拉线那样倾斜固定。

cues.en: But that's better than okay, because they don't all have to run out at the same angles,
cues.zh: 但这反而更好，因为缆绳不必都以完全相同的角度延伸出去，

cues.en: So you could have wires stretching a few 100 kilometers off to connect straight to cities and those can be quite solid wires you could run cable cars up, or scaled up enough, entire trains.
cues.zh: 所以你可以让缆索延伸数百公里直接连接到各大城市，这些缆索可以非常坚固，能在上面运行缆车；如果规模足够大，甚至能开整列火车。

cues.en: They can just move at normal speeds too, like any train or tram, not causing sonic booms or threatening to blow up cities if they fall off.
cues.zh: 它们也能以普通速度行驶，就像普通的火车或有轨电车一样，不会产生音爆，万一脱轨也不会有炸毁城市的风险。

cues.en: You could build wide platforms up there with domes and people could walk around on them just like on Earth, since there is gravity.
cues.zh: 你可以在上面建造带有穹顶的宽阔平台，因为存在重力，人们可以像在地球上一样在上面走动。

cues.en: You could hang structures from them too, like the Analama Tower, now suspended from a cable only 80 kilometers long not tens of thousands.
cues.zh: 你还可以在上面悬挂建筑物，比如 Analama Tower，现在只需悬挂在一条仅 80 公里长、而非数万公里的缆绳上即可。

cues.en: Indeed, so long as you keep a vacuum in that conduit, you could hang the ring just over mountain height.
cues.zh: 事实上，只要保持管道内部真空，你甚至可以把环悬挂在刚超过山峰的高度。

cues.en: You could put massive solar farms or regular farms up there and bring that power or food down to Earth. You can bring all the mass you want up from Earth for no more cost than the production and maintenance cost of the cable cars and solar panels powering it.
cues.zh: 你可以在上面建造巨型太阳能农场或普通农场，再把电力或食物运回地球。你想从地球运多少物资上去都行，成本仅相当于缆车和供电太阳能电池板的生产与维护费用。

cues.en: Nor does that inner spinning element need to necessarily be a wire under lots of strain if you spin it up too fast, you could use big particle accelerators.
cues.zh: 而且内部的旋转构件也不一定非得是转速过快而承受巨大应力的缆线，你可以使用大型粒子加速器。

cues.en: But this brings up another important point, what you do once you're up there.
cues.zh: 但这引出了另一个关键问题：一旦上去了，你要做什么？

cues.en: Truth be told, you don't need any other applications.
cues.zh: 说实话，你甚至不需要任何其他额外用途。

cues.en: An orbital ring of this type lets you zip around the planet and up to orbital heights and down to other spots quite cheaply,
cues.zh: 这种轨道环能让你以极低的成本绕着地球穿梭，上升到轨道高度，再下降到其他地点，

cues.en: but you are just at orbital height, not orbital speeds.
cues.zh: 但你只是处于轨道高度，并没有达到轨道速度。

cues.en: Step off the ring and you will fall down, though you will just fall down not reenter.
cues.zh: 只要走出环外你就会往下掉，不过你只是单纯下坠，并不会经历再入大气层的剧烈摩擦。

cues.en: So if you have a pressure suit, oxygen mask, and a parachute,
cues.zh: 所以只要你穿上压力服，戴上氧气面罩，背上降落伞，

cues.en: you could survive.
cues.zh: 你就能活下来。

cues.en: I imagine ring diving would be a popular sport.
cues.zh: 我想“跳环运动”可能会成为一项热门极限运动。

cues.en: Why are these good for space though?
cues.zh: 不过，为什么它们对航天探索大有裨益呢？

cues.en: Recall that when we discussed mass drivers,
cues.zh: 回想一下我们之前讨论质量投射器时，

cues.en: I said the track needed to be mostly straight because at orbital speeds your turning radius is huge, unless you want to be pancaked by centrifugal force when you turn.
cues.zh: 我说过轨道必须基本笔直，因为在轨道速度下转弯半径极大，除非你想在转弯时被离心力压成肉饼。

cues.en: Mass drivers and Lofstrom loops had to be thousands of kilometers long just to allow three g acceleration to normal orbital speed.
cues.zh: 质量投射器和 Lofstrom loop 必须长达数千公里，才允许以 3g 的加速度加速到常规轨道速度。

cues.en: They need to be much longer if you only want to do one g, normal Earth gravity.
cues.zh: 如果只想承受 1g（即正常的地球重力），轨道就必须长得多。

cues.en: But an orbital ring offers us a couple of unique advantages.
cues.zh: 但轨道环为我们提供了几项独特的优势。

cues.en: First off, it goes around the entire planet,
cues.zh: 首先，它环绕整个行星，

cues.en: so that is your turning radius if you're trying to build up speed to launch away from the Earth. Totally non coincidentally,
cues.zh: 所以如果你想加速飞离地球，这就是你的转弯半径。绝非巧合，

cues.en: the turning radius for an object at that altitude for one gee of acceleration
cues.zh: 在那个高度上，以 1G 加速度运动时的转弯半径

cues.en: is exactly orbital speed, that's why you are on free fall when orbiting.
cues.zh: 对应的速度恰好就是轨道速度——这就是为什么在轨道上时你处于自由落体。

cues.en: Now centrifugal turning force acts outward, while gravity pulls inward.
cues.zh: 离心转向力向外作用，而引力向内拉。

cues.en: So a ring around the planet has those two forces in opposite directions.
cues.zh: 所以，环绕行星的环上，这两个力方向相反。

cues.en: That means if we strap a vehicle to the ring and start speeding it up running around in circles,
cues.zh: 这意味着，如果我们把飞行器绑到环上，让它绕圈加速，

cues.en: the force of gravity is cancelling out that centrifugal force.
cues.zh: 引力就会抵消那个离心力。

cues.en: Indeed, if we were pulling two gees of acceleration,
cues.zh: 事实上，如果加速度拉到 2G，

cues.en: we could stand on the ceiling of our vehicle, or just flip it over, and feel like normal gravity only upside down.
cues.zh: 我们就能站在飞行器的天花板上，或者干脆把它翻过来，感觉就像正常重力，只是上下颠倒。

cues.en: We could build up to 11 kilometers a second like that, the escape velocity of Earth.
cues.zh: 这样我们就能加速到每秒 11 公里，也就是地球的逃逸速度。

cues.en: Eight kilometers a second will get you into orbit, but it takes 11 to escape out past the Moon. Those ground based systems like mass drivers and launch loops usually aim for three g's as pretty safe for most people.
cues.zh: 每秒 8 公里能让你进入轨道，但要飞出月球之外需要每秒 11 公里。像质量驱动器和发射环这类地面系统，通常把 3G 视为对大多数人相当安全的目标。

cues.en: With gravity cancelling out one of that, we could do four on the ring,
cues.zh: 引力能抵消掉其中 1G，所以我们在环上可以做到 4G，

cues.en: and be doing 16 kilometers a second when we release the ring, at whatever point we want, it is a circular track after all so we can do loops,
cues.zh: 并在从环上释放时达到每秒 16 公里，想在哪个点释放都行，毕竟这是圆形轨道，所以我们可以绕圈，

cues.en: and fly off at 16 kilometers a second, a decent speed for interplanetary
cues.zh: 并以每秒 16 公里的速度飞出去，这个速度对行星际

cues.en: travel even if you don't have rockets to help, which you would since you can bring all the fuel you want up to that ring.
cues.zh: 旅行来说相当不错——即使没有火箭帮忙；而你会有火箭，因为你可以把想要的燃料都带到那个环上。

cues.en: Most of the solar system is reasonably close to in line with our own equator,
cues.zh: 太阳系的大部分都相当接近与我们的赤道共面，

cues.en: so you are fairly close to the right direction north or south when you let go of an orbital ring around the equator. But these rings don't have to be around the equator, they can be at whatever angle. You could have another one at a different angle just above or below your own and take an elevator to it, or to another one even further up.
cues.zh: 所以，从赤道轨道环上释放时，你的方向已经相当接近正确方向，无论偏北还是偏南。但这些环不必在赤道周围，可以任意角度。你可以在自己的环上方或下方不远处再建一个不同角度的环，坐电梯到它那里，或者去更上方的另一个环。

cues.en: So you can take off from Earth even faster if you don't mind doing more gees, and freight can handle a lot more than passengers.
cues.zh: 所以，如果你不介意承受更多 G，就能从地球更快起飞；而货物能承受的 G 比乘客多得多。

cues.en: And you can also take off from a ring further up. As you get further from Earth, you lose a bit of that gravity advantage canceling things out, but you gain more turning radius and you are further up in the gravity well and won't lose as much speed leaving it. You can build as many rings as you please at any angle or height you want, and so long as the space between the two rings isn't so high that a cable between them would need to be super strong, you just take the elevator to the next ring up.
cues.zh: 你也可以从更上方的环起飞。离地球越远，你用来抵消重力的那点优势会减少一些，但转弯半径更大，而且在重力势阱中位置更高，离开时损失的速度也更少。你可以按任意角度或高度建任意多的环；只要两个环之间的间距不至于高到让它们之间的缆绳必须超级结实，你就可以坐电梯去下一个环。

cues.en: Out at geostationary,
cues.zh: 在地球同步轨道上，

cues.en: kilometers from the center of Earth, there's not much gravity left, but one gee of acceleration will get you 20 kilometers per second of speed, and four gees will get you 40 kilometers a second. That's the escape velocity from the solar system,
cues.zh: 公里，距地心这么远，剩下的重力已经不多了；但1个g的加速度能让你达到每秒20公里，4个g能到每秒40公里。这就是飞出太阳系的逃逸速度，

cues.en: and that is 3,500,000
cues.zh: 也就是350万

cues.en: kilometers a day. Not a bad interplanetary speed even if you were only using fuel to slow down.
cues.zh: 公里每天。就算只靠燃料减速，这个行星际速度也相当不错。

cues.en: This doesn't include the Earth's own orbital speed around the Sun either, of about 30 kilometers a second, which is quite a nice boost since everything further from the Sun is moving slower.
cues.zh: 这还没算上地球绕太阳约每秒30公里的轨道速度；离太阳越远，速度越慢，所以这是个相当不错的助推。

cues.en: You don't have to stop there either, you could build these rings all the way out to the Moon and beyond,
cues.zh: 你也不必止步于此，还可以把这些环一路建到月球甚至更远，

cues.en: and you could fly off from those at 60 or 120 kilometers a second, for one and four g respectively,
cues.zh: 从那些环上起飞，分别对应1个g和4个g，可达到每秒60或120公里，

cues.en: having never burned a drop of fuel, sailing out at 14,000,000
cues.zh: 而且一滴燃料都不用烧，就能以1400万

cues.en: kilometers a day, a speed that will get you to Mars at its average distance from us in ten days.
cues.zh: 公里每天的速度航行；按火星与我们的平均距离，十天就能到。

cues.en: You can slow down with these too, in the same way. You are not touching the ring when speeding up, you are using electromagnetic propulsion to avoid friction, and you don't need to touch it to slow down either.
cues.zh: 你也可以用这些环以同样的方式减速。加速时你并不接触环，而是用电磁推进避免摩擦；减速时同样不需要接触它。

cues.en: Indeed, you could just have something running around on the ring at that speed shoot a tether out to harpoon an incoming ship and slow it and you down the same way you sped up, so long as the tether is decently strong.
cues.zh: 事实上，你可以让环上某个以该速度运行的东西射出一根系绳，像鱼叉一样抓住迎面而来的飞船，然后像加速时那样把飞船和你一起减速——只要系绳足够结实。

cues.en: The exterior shell of a ring doesn't have to be stationary either, you could forgo the sheath or even have the sheath spinning and the inner wire staying stationary.
cues.zh: 环的外壳也不必静止；你可以不要护套，甚至让护套旋转、而内部导线保持静止。

cues.en: A ring like that next to a stationary ring might have some advantages for moving ships too, you match speeds with your train and jump on over.
cues.zh: 这样一个环挨着一个静止环，对转运飞船也可能有优势：你先和自己的列车速度匹配，再跳过去。

cues.en: Those cables in the atmosphere connecting the ring or the bottom ring to Earth would tend to be pretty numerous since any town who could afford one within a couple 100 kilometers of a ring would probably want one.
cues.zh: 大气层中连接环或底部环与地球的那些缆索会非常多，因为环周围两三百公里内，任何买得起的城镇大概都想要一根。

cues.en: You really don't need to worry about wind or lightning in these things but you can just attach them or reel them in during bad storms.
cues.zh: 这些缆索其实不用操心风或闪电，遇到大风暴直接固定住或收回就行。

cues.en: The rings only need a little force to keep them from wobbling so even a few cables is enough, and you'd have hundreds if not thousands connecting to each ring, so reeling some in during storms is no big deal.
cues.zh: 环只需要很小的力就能防止晃动，所以几根缆索就够了；而每个环会有数百甚至数千根缆索连接，风暴时收回一些根本不算事。

cues.en: I imagine by now you can start seeing why I always refer to orbital rings like a whole different level of space launch technology,
cues.zh: 我想你现在开始能明白，为什么我总把轨道环说成是整整另一个层次的太空发射技术，

cues.en: and we aren't done with the cool advantages yet.
cues.zh: 而且这些酷炫优势还没讲完。

cues.en: But so far we've mostly been talking about small ones, or just their use alone or with other rings.
cues.zh: 但到目前为止，我们主要谈的还是小型环，或者它们单独使用、或与其他环配合使用的情况。

cues.en: Before we scale up and talk hybrids,
cues.zh: 在我们扩大规模、讨论混合方案之前，

cues.en: let's talk safety and cost.
cues.zh: 先聊聊安全与成本。

cues.en: As to safety, for the smaller ones, that inner ring is spinning faster than orbital speeds, so if it gets damaged and flies out, probably shredding part of the ring in the process, it will fly out not down,
cues.zh: 先说安全。对较小的那些来说，内环的旋转速度比轨道速度还快，所以一旦损坏并甩飞出去——过程中很可能撕碎环的一部分——它会向外飞，而不是向下掉，

cues.en: and those bits which don't will burn up in reentry.
cues.zh: 而那些没飞出去的碎片，会在再入时烧毁。

cues.en: The stationary part will just fall, but as with previous systems we can attach explosive charges to break it into smaller bits and let parachutes slow those down.
cues.zh: 静止部分则只会坠落，但和之前的系统一样，我们可以装上炸药把它炸成更小的碎片，再用降落伞减速。

cues.en: That option is totally out the window for the bigger ones we will get to in a moment, but those are much sturdier since they'd have tons of rings that supported them, not just one.
cues.zh: 这个方案对稍后要讲到的更大结构完全不可行，不过那些结构要坚固得多，因为它们会有大量环来支撑，而不只靠一个环。

cues.en: As an example of hybrid tech though, while we can place another ring right below and at an angle to a ring so that it might fall to rest on its neighbor, we can also use the Atlas Pillars from last episode to run straight up beneath the ring like normal support pylons,
cues.zh: 不过作为混合技术的一个例子：我们可以把另一个环放在某个环的正下方并成一定角度，让它可能落下搭在相邻环上；也可以用上一集的 Atlas Pillars，像普通支撑塔一样从环下方直直向上延伸，

cues.en: though they need not run up straight either.
cues.zh: 不过它们也不必竖直向上延伸。

cues.en: Of course you could just bypass the internal spinning rings or particles with these, just one big suspension bridge running around the planet or just partway,
cues.zh: 当然，你也可以用这些结构直接绕过内部的旋转环或粒子，只造一座绕行星一整圈或只绕一部分的大型悬索桥，

cues.en: or even at angles,
cues.zh: 甚至以一定角度布置，

cues.en: but the ring is better and the Atlas Pillars just allow a nice addition of capacity and safety.
cues.zh: 但轨道环本身更好，而 Atlas Pillars 只是很好地增加了承载能力和安全性。

cues.en: As to cost, that's another story.
cues.zh: 至于成本，那就是另一回事了。

cues.en: Once the first ring is in place, you can use it to bring all the rest up quite cheaply, but that first ring probably needs to be fairly sturdy and mass at least several thousand tons.
cues.zh: 一旦第一个环就位，你就可以用它相当便宜地把其余部分运上去，但第一个环可能需要相当坚固，质量至少几千吨。

cues.en: So it is essentially the same price range as bringing up a basic space elevator,
cues.zh: 所以它的价格区间基本和建一个基础太空电梯相当，

cues.en: same concept too. You get a simple small one up and use it to bring more mass up. More expensive than a space elevator though since those assume super strong and super light materials,
cues.zh: 概念也一样。你先弄上去一个简单的小环，再用它运更多质量上去。不过它比太空电梯更贵，因为太空电梯假定使用超强又超轻的材料，

cues.en: and the orbital ring is just copper or iron, cheap but expensive to get into space.
cues.zh: 而轨道环只是铜或铁，材料便宜，但送入太空很贵。

cues.en: This is one of the reasons mining and industrializing the Moon, with its huge quantities of raw materials and negligible gravity and atmosphere,
cues.zh: 这也是为什么开采月球并使其工业化——月球有海量原材料、重力和大气可忽略——

cues.en: is very attractive to us.
cues.zh: 对我们非常有吸引力。

cues.en: It is just as useful, indeed arguably more so, even with an orbital ring making freight costs up from Earth cheaper, but it makes it far easier to build that first orbital ring, especially if you want it be a decently large and handy one.
cues.zh: 它同样有用，甚至可以说更有用，即使轨道环让从地球往上的货运成本更便宜，但它让建造第一个轨道环容易得多，尤其是如果你想要一个相当大且好用的环。

cues.en: I would be a lot more confident bootstrapping
cues.zh: 我会更有信心通过自举

cues.en: more rings from a first orbital ring a meter or more thick massing a couple tons per meter of length than a hair thin wire,
cues.zh: 从一个每米质量几吨、一米或更厚的第一轨道环，扩展出更多环，而不是从一根细如发丝的线缆开始，

cues.en: And at a circumference of 40,000,000 meters,
cues.zh: 而在周长 40,000,000 米的情况下，

cues.en: such a ring would mass in around a 100 megatons,
cues.zh: 这样的环质量约为 1 亿吨，

cues.en: more mass than everything we've lifted to orbit combined.
cues.zh: 比我们送入轨道的所有东西加起来还重。

cues.en: But better to start that way, and so better to use the earlier and more modern systems we've discussed to get to the moon and asteroids first.
cues.zh: 但最好还是先从那步开始，利用我们之前讨论过的那些更现代的早期系统，先登上月球和小行星。

cues.en: When colonizing the West Coast, you start with the Oregon Trail,
cues.zh: 就像当年开拓美西，得先从俄勒冈小道走起，

cues.en: not a massive three lane interstate freeway after all.
cues.zh: 毕竟不可能一上来就建一条宽阔的三车道州际高速。

cues.en: So this is definitely not your next step in making space cheap.
cues.zh: 所以，要降低太空探索成本，这绝不是你的下一步。

cues.en: Nothing offers cheaper cost per kilogram launched,
cues.zh: 论单位公斤的发射成本，确实没有比它更低的了，

cues.en: but it takes a lot to set up, and its real advantage is throughput,
cues.zh: 但它的前期投入极大，而且它真正的优势在于吞吐量，

cues.en: not cost per item launched.
cues.zh: 而不是单次发射的成本。

cues.en: Only the space elevator even gets into the ballpark with orbital rings on that score, and that does require materials
cues.zh: 在这方面，唯有太空电梯能与轨道环相提并论，但这需要我们目前

cues.en: we don't really have.
cues.zh: 根本没有的材料。

cues.en: The orbital ring on the other hand, while quite a feat of engineering in every respect,
cues.zh: 而另一方面，轨道环虽然在各方面都堪称工程奇迹，

cues.en: relies on only modern tech, though a power source like fusion and access to room temperature superconductors
cues.zh: 却只需要现代技术；尽管如果能用上核聚变电源和室温超导体，

cues.en: makes it a lot better.
cues.zh: 体验还会大幅提升。

cues.en: You don't just build one either, you build a bunch at different angles around the planet with cables running off to any place that wants one.
cues.zh: 而且你不仅建一个，还可以在地球周围以不同角度建很多个，引出缆线连接任何需要的地方。

cues.en: The Orbital Ring Network makes a nice launch point for interplanetary
cues.zh: 轨道环网络不仅是行星际旅行的绝佳起点，

cues.en: travel, but it's even more phenomenal for intra planetary travel.
cues.zh: 用于全球范围内的行星内旅行更是惊艳。

cues.en: You take a cable from your town to orbit at whatever speed local law permits,
cues.zh: 你可以从自家小镇搭乘缆车直达轨道，速度取决于当地法规，

cues.en: arriving in less than an hour even if it's a wide angle, long cable and limited to subsonic speeds,
cues.zh: 即便角度平缓、缆线更长且限速亚音速，也用不了一小时就能到达，

cues.en: and from there race around to your exit ramp at hypersonic velocities.
cues.zh: 接着便能以高超音速疾驰到你的出口匝道。

cues.en: If those rings are big enough and those cables sturdy enough,
cues.zh: 如果这些环足够宽大、缆线足够坚固，

cues.en: it's not just passengers traveling anywhere on the globe in a couple hours,
cues.zh: 不仅乘客能在几小时内抵达全球任意角落，

cues.en: it's bulk freight by the megaton doing it too.
cues.zh: 数以百万吨计的大宗货物也能做到。

cues.en: Scared up, one of these ring networks can handle billions of people and billions of tons of cargo moving to and from space every day.
cues.zh: 规模扩大后，这样的一套环网每天能运送数十亿人和数十亿吨物资往返太空。

cues.en: And you really can scale these up too. That guy wire going to the ring could instead be a big highway with a dome tunnel over it you could drive your car up. Those rings don't have to be meters wide but could be kilometers.
cues.zh: 而且它的规模确实可以大幅拓展。通往轨道环的拉索甚至可以换成带穹顶隧道的宽阔公路，让你直接开车上去。环本身的宽度也不必局限在几米，完全可以达到几千米。

cues.en: And if they are low enough in the atmosphere to gain some protection from meteors and space trash, which you are at 80 kilometers up, you could just dome over places and walk around with regular old air, sunlight, and gravity.
cues.zh: 如果它们的大气高度足够低，能抵御流星和太空垃圾——比如在80千米的高空——你完全可以在上面罩上穹顶，在正常的空气、阳光和重力下漫步。

cues.en: You wouldn't have to stop your car drive when you arrived either, or your walk.
cues.zh: 到达之后，你无论是开车还是散步，都不必停下来。

cues.en: People ask sometimes about being able to connect a space elevator straight from the Moon to Earth, and you can't even with a super strong material because the Moon is tidally locked to Earth but not the other way around.
cues.zh: 有人常问能不能建一座直接连通地球与月球的太空电梯，但哪怕有强度极高的材料也做不到，因为月球被地球潮汐锁定，反过来却并非如此。

cues.en: You can do that with Pluto and Cheren for instance since they are both locked to each other and always show the same face.
cues.zh: 但比如冥王星和卡戎就可以，因为它们相互锁定，永远以同一面相对。

cues.en: With an orbital ring, you actually can do this. Orbital rings don't have to be perfect circles for one thing but that's not what I mean.
cues.zh: 有了轨道环，你确实可以做到这点。首先，轨道环不一定非得是完美的圆形，但我指的不是这个。

cues.en: You've got a stationary ring around Earth, just above the atmosphere or way out at geostationary
cues.zh: 比如在地球周围建一个静止的环，可以紧贴大气层上方，或者远在地球同步轨道，

cues.en: or even further.
cues.zh: 甚至更远的地方。

cues.en: Once you're up at geo though, the strength of gravity is so low you don't need strong materials for thousand kilometer long tethers anymore,
cues.zh: 但一旦到达地球同步轨道，引力就变得非常弱，连接上千公里的缆绳不再需要极高强度的材料，

cues.en: so you could easily build one up from the ring out to the moon's orbit.
cues.zh: 所以你可以很轻松地从环上延伸出一条缆绳，一直通向月球轨道。

cues.en: We could put a ring there too, but more importantly we could have an elevator come off the moon stretching all the way to the ring at geostationary.
cues.zh: 我们也可以在月球那里建一个环，但更重要的是，我们可以建一部太空电梯，从月球一路延伸到地球同步轨道的环上。

cues.en: That ring sheath doesn't need to be moving at normal geostationary
cues.zh: 那个环的外壳不需要以常规的地球同步

cues.en: speed, nor does the tether to the moon have to stay fixed. You don't even need fancy magnetic connections either. The moon only goes one kilometer a second. We can actually make traditional mechanical connections that can handle such things.
cues.zh: 速度运行，通往月球的缆绳也不需要固定死。你甚至不需要花哨的磁力连接。月球的速度只有每秒一公里，我们完全可以用传统的机械连接来搞定。

cues.en: So yes, with an orbital ring network, a big one but not a high-tech one, you could grab a train from your hometown wherever on Earth and step out of it on the moon somewhere.
cues.zh: 所以没错，借助一个轨道环网络——规模很大但技术并不超前——你可以从地球老家的任何地方坐上火车，然后直接在月球的某个地方下车。

cues.en: I imagine you'd just take a ship from the first ring instead or one of the higher ones closer to geostationary.
cues.zh: 不过我想大家可能更愿意直接从第一层环坐飞船，或者从更靠近地球同步轨道的更高层环出发。

cues.en: Those already offer launch speeds fast enough to let you make that trip in under a day. The four g shot off a geostationary one would get you there in three hours,
cues.zh: 那些环提供的发射速度已经足够快，让你能在一天之内抵达。如果是从地球同步轨道的环上以 4G 加速度发射，三个小时就能到，

cues.en: but you could actually walk from Earth to the Moon with this network,
cues.zh: 但借助这个网络，你确实可以直接从地球“走”到月球，

cues.en: though you'd need magnetic boots once you got far from Earth's gravity well. Though you could also make the connection between the rings be hollow spinning tubes with spin gravity too.
cues.zh: 虽然远离地球引力势阱后你需要穿磁力靴。当然，你也可以把环之间的连接通道做成中空的旋转管道，利用自转产生人工重力。

cues.en: You can also scale this up to go between planets,
cues.zh: 你甚至可以把这个体系放大，用于行星际通行，

cues.en: a bit silly but possible.
cues.zh: 听起来有点离谱，但确实可行。

cues.en: I remember some years back before I started the channel and used to play with more extreme forms of megastructures,
cues.zh: 我记得几年前开这个频道之前，我经常琢磨一些更极端的巨型结构，

cues.en: not the ones we've covered on the channel, those are all basic ones, even the solar system sized ones, I tried coming up with a way to walk, swim, sail, or fly between planets
cues.zh: 不是我们在频道里讲过的那些，那些都算基础款，哪怕是太阳系尺度的也一样；我当时试图构想出一种在行星之间步行、游泳、航海或飞行的方法，

cues.en: and orbital rings and dynamic structures
cues.zh: 而轨道环和动态结构

cues.en: do actually let you do crazy stuff like that.
cues.zh: 确实能让你实现这种疯狂的设想。

cues.en: More down to Earth, literally, they do let you wake up in the morning at home and commute to space for work,
cues.zh: 更实际一点说，字面意义上的，它们确实能让你早上在家里醒来，然后通勤去太空上班，

cues.en: and you can make a lot of living space in low orbit too.
cues.zh: 而且你还可以在低轨道上建造大量的居住空间。

cues.en: There's a game setting called Warhammer 40 k or 40,000
cues.zh: 有一个名为 Warhammer 40K（战锤 40,000）的游戏设定，

cues.en: set in the year 40000.
cues.zh: 背景设定在公元 40000 年。

cues.en: Many of you are probably already familiar with it and it features Earth, called Terra in that, as a galactic capital home to trillions, an example of an ecumenopolis which we've discussed before.
cues.zh: 你们很多人可能已经很熟悉了，那里的地球被称为泰拉（Terra），作为银河首都居住着数万亿人口，是典型的“全城球”（ecumenopolis），我们之前也讨论过。

cues.en: In that there's something mentioned called orbital plate,
cues.zh: 设定中提到了一种叫做“轨道板块”（orbital plate）的东西，

cues.en: which is described as a small continent floating over the planet, and they've got several.
cues.zh: 它被描述为悬浮在星球上空的小型大陆，而且他们有好几个。

cues.en: No real details are given about them or how they hang out there, they do have anti gravity in that series though so probably that,
cues.zh: 关于它们或者它们怎么悬在那里的细节并没有交代，不过那部剧里确实有反重力技术，所以大概就是靠那个吧，

cues.en: But orbital rings let you do stuff like that.
cues.zh: 但轨道环确实能让你做到这种事。

cues.en: Indeed, you could stick a bunch of them all wide and at different angles and slightly different height up over a planet to totally enclose it. Lay down some mesh and some dirt and water and air and you've got a new planetary surface.
cues.zh: 确实，你可以在行星上空放上一堆不同角度、不同高度的宽环，把整颗星球彻底包起来。铺上网格，填上泥土、水和空气，你就拥有了一个崭新的行星表面。

cues.en: You could do something like that around a gas giant like Saturn and produce what is called a super mundane planet or shellworld.
cues.zh: 你也可以在土星这样的气态巨行星周围这么做，打造出所谓的“超凡行星”或“壳层世界”（Shellworld）。

cues.en: You could do several concentric shells around Earth and produce what we call a Matrioshka
cues.zh: 你还可以在地球周围套上几层同心壳，打造出我们所说的套娃式

cues.en: Shellworld,
cues.zh: 壳层世界，

cues.en: both of which are discussed in the episode Shellworlds from a couple years back.
cues.zh: 这两者都在几年前那期关于壳层世界的节目中讨论过。

cues.en: I was going to say with orbital rings the sky's the limit as to what you can do but that's not really a good saying considering the sky is specifically not the limit with them. If you've got enough power and can use it without too much waste heat being produced, basically if you've got good superconductors and fusion, you can build some truly monstrous stuff.
cues.zh: 我本来想说有了轨道环，你能做的事情是“上不封顶”，但这么说其实不太贴切，因为对它们来说天空根本不是上限。只要你有足够的能量，并且利用它时不会产生过多废热——基本上只要有优秀的超导体和核聚变——你就能造出一些真正庞大骇人的奇观。

cues.en: Particularly since the Atlas Pillar variation we discussed last time lets you make straight lines not just curves,
cues.zh: 尤其是我们上次讨论的 Atlas 柱变体，它不仅能做弧线，还能做直线，

cues.en: and orbital rings don't have to be circles,
cues.zh: 而且轨道环并不非得是正圆形，

cues.en: and you can change these things dimensions,
cues.zh: 你还可以改变这些结构的尺寸，

cues.en: that's part of why we call them dynamic structures.
cues.zh: 这也是我们称它们为动态结构的原因之一。

cues.en: I think by now you can see why I saved orbital rings for last,
cues.zh: 我想大家现在应该明白，我为什么把轨道环留到最后了吧，

cues.en: and why I've spent the whole series talking about how much more awesome they are than the other concepts for getting stuff into space cheaper and safer.
cues.zh: 也明白了我为什么在整个系列里都在讲，比起其他更便宜、更安全进入太空的概念，轨道环有多么不可思议。

cues.en: Now I'm not formally closing out the Upward Bound series, we may revisit it more in the future. We've got tons of concepts we haven't covered yet and others we could cover in more detail that just shared an episode with a few other related concepts.
cues.zh: 现在我并没有正式完结 Upward Bound 系列，我们以后可能还会继续聊。我们还有很多未曾涉及的概念，也有一些之前和其他概念挤在同一期里、还可以更详细展开的概念。

cues.en: However, this ends the series for now and the main sequence sequence of it.
cues.zh: 不过，这个系列以及它的主线内容目前就先告一段落了。

cues.en: We've looked at space elevators and skyhooks and mass drivers.
cues.zh: 我们探讨过了太空电梯、天钩和质量投射器。

cues.en: We've talked about ways to improve rockets by making them reusable or giving them better power sources like atomic ones or metallic hydrogen.
cues.zh: 我们聊过了如何改进火箭——比如让它们可复用，或者采用核动力、金属氢等更好的能量来源。

cues.en: We've looked at thousand kilometer long floating launch loops and runways suspended from towers so tall they don't just scrape the sky but rise over it. Now, finally, we see the orbital ring.
cues.zh: 我们看过了上千公里长的悬浮发射环，以及悬挂在高塔上的跑道——那些塔高到不仅是直插云霄，而是早已耸立在天空之上。现在，我们终于见识到了轨道环。

cues.en: I don't know what technologies we will see in between modern rocketry and this concept,
cues.zh: 我不知道在现代火箭技术与这个概念之间，我们还会见证哪些技术诞生，

cues.en: but barring a big game changer like anti gravity or wormholes we can open up from planet to planet like in Stargate,
cues.zh: 但除非出现像反重力，或者像 Stargate 里那样能在行星之间开启虫洞等颠覆性的重大变革，

cues.en: I think this one is the final product of the effort to get people off the ground and up to the heavens.
cues.zh: 否则我认为，轨道环就是人类为了离开地面、飞向深空所做努力的终极形态。

cues.en: Even things like cheap compact fusion we could make space planes with doesn't really rival this in terms of volume because those will produce so much thrust and heat that you could never use millions of them a day on the planet.
cues.zh: 就算是能用廉价紧凑型聚变造出太空飞机，在体量上也远远比不上这个，因为那会产生巨大的推力和热量，地球上根本不可能每天用上几百万架。

cues.en: This system doesn't just get you into space cheap, it gets your whole civilization up there cheap and lets you truly engage in bulk trade and transport.
cues.zh: 这个系统不仅能让你廉价地进入太空，还能让整个文明廉价地上太空，让你真正实现大规模的贸易和运输。

cues.en: And that's always been the real goal, not to get a few astronauts to Mars, but to make it so cheap and easy that going to the Moon is like flying to another country and going to another planet takes as much time and money as an ocean cruise.
cues.zh: 这才是真正的目标：不是把几个宇航员送上火星，而是让它便宜到、容易到去月球就像飞另一个国家，去另一个行星的时间和花费就像坐一次海上邮轮。

cues.en: So that's the series wrap up on Upward Bound, getting into space.
cues.zh: 以上就是《Upward Bound》系列“进入太空”部分的总结。

cues.en: If those giant megastructures like Shellworlds caught your interest, I suggest trying the megastructures playlist.
cues.zh: 如果你对壳世界（Shellworlds）这类巨型结构感兴趣，我建议你看看巨型结构播放列表。

cues.en: Though you can skip the first three episodes since those are just quick overviews of what we covered in more detail in this series.
cues.zh: 不过前三集可以跳过，因为那些只是快速概览，本系列已经讲得更详细了。

cues.en: Those are older episodes, so the graphics and audio quality are a lot lower, but the meat and potatoes are still there. If you're interested in some of the civilization aspects of folks who could build orbital rings, try the advanced civilization series, starting with Arcologies.
cues.zh: 那些是比较老的剧集，画面和音质差不少，但核心内容还在。如果你对能造轨道环的文明社会层面感兴趣，可以看高级文明系列，从《Arcologies》开始。

cues.en: If you want to continue on past leaving this planet, try the Life in a Space Colony series.
cues.zh: 如果你想继续看离开地球之后的内容，可以看《太空殖民地中的生活》系列。

cues.en: For alerts when new episodes come out, make sure to subscribe to the channel. And if you enjoyed this episode, hit the like button and share it with others.
cues.zh: 想在新剧集发布时收到提醒，请务必订阅频道。如果你喜欢这集，请点赞并分享给其他人。

cues.en: Until next time, thanks for watching, and have a great week.
cues.zh: 下次见，感谢观看，祝你这周愉快。
